newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cuts official cash rate to 5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cuts official cash rate to 5.0 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said on Wednesday that it had cut its official cash rate by 50 basis points to 5.0 percent.
This is the fifth monetary policy easing by the central bank in the last 12 months, each of 50 basis points.

The latest reduction had been expected by financial markets for most of July since the central bank board held its monthly board meeting on July 1. Bond yields and the Australian dollar had fallen in anticipation of another easing.
Markets had forecast that while a rate cut was likely, it would probably not be announced until after the next monthly board meeting set for August 5.

The RBA said that while financial markets spent a lot of time picking when a rate cut would be announced, it had never been the central bank's standard practice to announce changes the day after a board meeting as this would limit flexibility.

Only eight of 22 changes since 1990 have occurred on the day following the board meeting. The bank said there seemed no point in delaying the implementation for another week, citing good CPI and wages data which led to a presumption of a further reduction in interest rates and also led to a further conferral with board members to seek their views on the timing and stance of policy.
